factual_methodology.summary: Federal Reserve, U.S. Treasury, ECB, BCB and B3 provide the primary policy, yield-curve, monetary and Brazilian market evidence. Intraday Treasury, oil and European sovereign observations are explicitly time-bounded and supported separately.

novelty.summary: The 7 October delta reverses the prior day's partial offset: oil and long yields are rising together again, while the 10-year Treasury reopening and FOMC minutes create same-day tests of duration demand and the Fed reaction function.

editorial_publication_readiness.summary: The brief separates official closing data from early-session observations, states the information cutoff, treats the FOMC minutes as backward-looking evidence rather than a forecast and avoids reading Brazil's post-election asset move as a confirmed fiscal regime.

contextual_depth.summary: The brief links energy, inflation uncertainty, Treasury supply, long-duration financing costs, French fiscal risk and Brazil's election repricing through explicit transmission mechanisms and invalidation conditions.

visual_evidence_readiness.signature: 1 evidence table + 2 explicit charts + 1 causal flow + 1 regional transmission map per locale
visual_evidence_readiness.summary: Visual floor for a brief is exceeded. Treasury yields are compared in common units across the prior official close and current early-session observations; France and Germany are compared on the same 10-year sovereign-yield scale; the flow and map encode mechanisms defended in prose.
visual_evidence_readiness.limitations: Intraday U.S., European and oil observations can move materially before the close. The France-Germany spread is not treated as a pure fiscal-risk measure.

contrary_evidence: A strong 10-year auction and lower post-auction yields would weaken the interpretation that duration supply is tightening financial conditions.
A renewed decline in Brent would restore part of the energy offset visible on 6 October.
The FOMC minutes describe a meeting held three weeks earlier and may carry less information than current inflation and labour data.
Brazil's stronger real and still-elevated equity level may persist even if the immediate post-election rally consolidates.
limitations: Market prices cited for 7 October are early-session observations and can change materially before the close.
The analysis does not treat the Treasury term premium as directly observed; it infers duration pressure from the curve, supply calendar and market behavior.
The France-Germany yield gap includes monetary, liquidity and market-structure effects in addition to country-specific fiscal risk.
The Focus report released on 5 October reflects responses collected before Brazil's first-round election and is used only as a pre-election benchmark.
notes: Approved for same-day publication with an 08:05 BRT information cutoff. EN/PT-BR factual parity, controlled geography/taxonomy and visual parity were checked.

en.title: Global Macro — oil and long yields rise together as Fed minutes and Treasury supply test financial conditions
en.deck: Oil is back above $101 while U.S. long yields return to multi-decade extremes, putting the 10-year Treasury reopening and FOMC minutes at the center of today's financial-conditions test.
en.regime: Energy and long-duration rates are tightening together again: oil is above $101 while the U.S. 10-year is near 5.32% and the 30-year near 5.71%, making Treasury demand and the Fed reaction function the immediate tests.
en.key_risk: Persistent co-movement between higher energy prices and higher long yields can tighten both operating margins and financing conditions before central banks change short-term policy rates.
